metadata.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II

problem_summary.summary: From a sorted singly linked list, remove every value that occurs more than once and retain only values appearing exactly once.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: possibly-null ListNode head. Return the filtered ListNode head. The judge supplies ListNode { int val; ListNode next; }.
constraints: The list is sorted in ascending order

brute_force.explanation: Count each value with a HashMap, then relink only nodes whose value has frequency one.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The frequency table identifies exactly the values that occur once. Keeping precisely their original nodes produces the required result while preserving sorted order.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) expected across counting and filtering.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(u) auxiliary for u distinct values in the map.

optimized.explanation: Use a dummy predecessor and scan equal-value runs. If a run has multiple nodes, skip the entire run; otherwise advance the predecessor to keep its single node.
optimized.correctness_idea: Sorted order makes every duplicate value a contiguous run. Detecting whether the next value differs identifies run length one; skipping longer runs removes all occurrences as required.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each node is examined and skipped at most once.

steps.condition: The next node is absent or has a different value.
steps.action: Keep 1 and move previous to it.

steps.condition: The next two nodes share value 2.
4 and 7 each form singleton runs; 5 occurs twice.
steps.action: Retain singleton links and bypass the duplicate run.

edge_cases.handling: Every run is skipped and the returned head is null.

edge_cases.case: A duplicate run starts at the head
edge_cases.handling: The dummy predecessor allows the head run to be removed.
Every node is retained in its existing order.
